headline: Data Centers Pay for Grid Upgrades
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for the increased electric generating capacity and transmission infrastructure costs they necessitate, preventing these costs from being passed to residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Consumer advocacy groups, utility watchdog organizations, Governor Spanberger, Senator Mark Warner, Delegate Jeion Ward
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups (implied)
news_headline: New Virginia Law Shifts Data Center Energy Costs
news_summary: New legislation in Virginia shifts energy costs to high-demand users, requiring facilities using 25 MW or more to pay for increased generating capacity and preventing these costs from being passed on to other customers. This aims to shield residential ratepayers from data center infrastructure costs.

headline: Mandatory Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and data collection for water resource planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, environmental groups, water resource planners
opponents: None explicitly stated, but potentially some data center operators (implied)
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Data Center Water Tracking
news_summary: Virginia lawmakers passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report water volumes provided to data centers, including potable and reclaimed water, to address concerns about the lack of centralized tracking of data center water use. This legislation aims to provide better data for policymakers and water resource planners to understand the industry's impact on Virginia's water resources.

headline: Local Control Over Data Center Siting
short_summary: This bill grants localities the authority to require site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including sound profiles and potential impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites, before approving rezoning or special permits.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Delegate Joshua E. Thomas, Delegate Elizabeth R. Guzman, Delegate Dan I. Helmer, Delegate John Chilton McAuliff, Delegate David A. Reid, Virginia League of Conservation Voters, environmental and conservation groups, neighborhood associations, historic preservation advocates, farmland protection groups, local planning and public health organizations
opponents: Data center developers and tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations, pro-growth business or utility groups (concerned about permitting delays and added costs)
news_headline: Virginia Law Requires Data Center Site Assessments
news_summary: Virginia's new law, HB 153, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools, and allows localities to require reviews of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites. This legislation aims to provide local governments with more tools for informed decision-making regarding data center development.
